title: Chemical Synthesis, Yield and Spectroscopy
seo_title: Year 12 Chemistry: Chemical Synthesis and Analysis Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)

meta_desc: Free Year 12 Chemistry worksheets on synthesis and analysis: percentage yield, atom economy, green chemistry, esters, mass spectra, infrared and NMR spectroscopy and chromatography. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Atom economy = mass of desired product ÷ mass of all products × 100.
body_html:
How to think about it

Chemists design syntheses for a high yield and a high atom economy, with safe, cheap and renewable inputs (green chemistry). Esters form from carboxylic acids and alcohols; reactions are often heated under reflux and the product purified by distillation.

Products are identified by instruments: mass spectrometry gives molar mass and fragments; infrared shows functional groups (O–H, C=O); NMR shows the carbon and hydrogen environments and splitting patterns; chromatography separates and identifies substances.

Example

Theoretical 12.0 g, actual 9.0 g. % yield?

9.0 ÷ 12.0 × 100

Answer: 75%

Example

Ethyl ethanoate: which acid and alcohol?

-oate from the acid

ethyl from the alcohol

Answer: ethanoic acid and ethanol

Common mistakes

  • Confusing percentage yield with atom economy.
  • Thinking the number of ¹³C NMR peaks equals the number of carbons.
  • Naming esters with the acid part first.

faq.q: Why can a reaction have a high yield but a low atom economy?
faq.a: Yield compares the product you got with the most possible; atom economy shows how much of the reactants end up in the product you want rather than in by-products.

faq.q: Which technique tells you the functional groups present?
faq.a: Infrared spectroscopy: bonds such as O–H, C=O and N–H absorb at characteristic wavenumbers.

items.q: 5.00 g of Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> gave 1.57 g of Fe (Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO<sub>2</sub>). Calculate the percentage yield.
items.e: Theoretical mass = 3.50 g; yield = 1.57 ÷ 3.50 × 100 = 45.0%.

items.q: What does an infrared spectrum show about an organic compound?
items.e: A broad O–H peak near 3300 cm⁻¹ shows an alcohol.

items.q: 100 g of Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> gave 66.4 g of Fe (Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO<sub>2</sub>). Calculate the percentage yield.
items.e: Theoretical mass = 69.9 g; yield = 66.4 ÷ 69.9 × 100 = 95.0%.

items.q: What is an esterification reaction?
c: a carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol to form an ester and water
items.e: Concentrated sulfuric acid is a catalyst.

items.q: Why do chemists consider yield, rate, cost and safety when designing an industrial process?
c: the best process gives enough product quickly, cheaply, safely and with little waste
items.e: This involves many compromises.

items.q: Why is biodiesel made from vegetable oils described as renewable?
c: it is made from crude oil
it produces no CO₂ at all
the oils come from crops that can be regrown
items.e: It is made by transesterification.

items.q: 100 g of N<sub>2</sub> reacts completely: N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> → 2NH<sub>3</sub>. Calculate the maximum (theoretical) mass of NH<sub>3</sub>.
items.e: n(N2) = 3.57 mol, n(NH3) = 7.14 mol, m = 121 g.

items.q: Calculate the percentage atom economy for making C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH by this reaction: C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> → 2C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH + 2CO<sub>2</sub>.
items.e: Atom economy = Mr of desired product ÷ total Mr of reactants × 100 = 92.00 ÷ 180.0 × 100 = 51.1%.

items.q: 5.00 g of Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> reacts completely: Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO<sub>2</sub>. Calculate the maximum (theoretical) mass of Fe.
items.e: n(Fe2O3) = 0.0313 mol, n(Fe) = 0.0627 mol, m = 3.50 g.

items.q: What is the percentage yield?
c: mass of product ÷ mass of reactants
items.e: Losses lower the yield.

items.q: What does chromatography (such as HPLC) separate substances by?
c: their different attraction to the stationary and mobile phases
items.e: Retention time identifies substances.

items.q: What is the purpose of heating under reflux?
c: to heat a reaction for a long time without losing volatile substances
items.e: Vapours condense and drip back.

items.q: Calculate the percentage atom economy for making Fe by this reaction: Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO<sub>2</sub>.
items.e: Atom economy = Mr of desired product ÷ total Mr of reactants × 100 = 111.6 ÷ 243.6 × 100 = 45.8%.

items.q: What does a mass spectrum's molecular ion peak (M⁺) tell you?
c: the number of carbon atoms only
the relative molecular mass of the compound
items.e: The highest m/z peak (ignoring isotopes).

items.q: What is the name of the ester made from ethanol and ethanoic acid?
items.e: Alcohol part first (-yl), acid part second (-oate).

items.q: Which reaction type always has 100% atom economy?
items.e: All atoms of the reactants end up in one product.

items.q: 12.0 g of N<sub>2</sub> reacts completely: N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> → 2NH<sub>3</sub>. Calculate the maximum (theoretical) mass of NH<sub>3</sub>.

20.0 g of C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> gave 7.36 g of C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH (C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> → 2C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH + 2CO<sub>2</sub>). Calculate the percentage yield.
items.e: Theoretical mass = 10.2 g; yield = 7.36 ÷ 10.2 × 100 = 72.0%.

items.e: n(Fe2O3) = 0.125 mol, n(Fe) = 0.251 mol, m = 14.0 g.

items.e: n(N2) = 1.79 mol, n(NH3) = 3.57 mol, m = 60.7 g.

items.q: Which splitting pattern is seen in the ¹H NMR spectrum of ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH?
items.e: Use the n + 1 rule: a peak splits into n + 1 lines where n is the number of H atoms on the adjacent carbon(s).

items.q: Which splitting pattern is seen in the ¹H NMR spectrum of bromoethane, CH₃CH₂Br?
items.e: Use the n + 1 rule: a peak splits into n + 1 lines where n is the number of H atoms on the adjacent carbon(s).

items.q: How many peaks are there in the ¹H NMR spectrum of propanoic acid, CH₃CH₂COOH?
items.e: Count the different hydrogen environments: 3 (triplet, quartet and singlet).

items.q: In ¹H NMR, a group of protons has 0 hydrogen atoms on the adjacent carbon atoms. What is its splitting pattern?
items.e: n + 1 rule: 0 + 1 = 1 lines.
